propositions: Event body data written to the store is never screened for embedded credentials, allowing live API keys, tokens, and service-account keys to be written to disk and auto-pushed to the shared tickets branch
Untrusted Jira-sourced COMMENT and EDIT events bypass the append_event seam by calling finalize_event's halves directly, leaving external input unscreened even if a screen existed at append_event

GitHub push protection's rejection of the tickets branch on a leaked Anthropic key caused a store-sharing outage (153 queued commits) for all concurrent sessions, with the failure surfacing only as transient contention warnings rather than a clear credential-leak diagnosis

A deterministic secret pattern detector must live at finalize_event (the single write seam all four write paths route through) and refuse writes matching high-confidence credential shapes, with an audited `--allow-secret-pattern=<reason>` override for false positives

The refusal path must not echo the secret value, credential fragments, or payload keys into exception messages, logs, stderr, or stored events, while the forced-write path records the reason and bypassed families on the event for auditability

Detection patterns are tuned by measurement (fixed-width windows, line-anchored PEM banners) to avoid greedy quantifier padding attacks and false positives on prose descriptions (regex literals, truncated placeholders), achieving zero real-world leaks and one recoverable false positive (AWS doc example) across 25,125 live events
